sections.overview: This large Southeast Asian cyprinid is a strongly migratory river fish of the Mekong and other regional drainages.
sections.identification: It is a robust barb known locally by several names, including Trey chhkok in Khmer and ca coc in Vietnamese.
sections.habitat: It occupies the Mekong main channel and large tributaries, moving between river reaches and downstream nursery areas.
sections.diet: Adults are omnivorous, taking molluscs, algae, worms, insects, crustaceans and sometimes fish; young fish feed mainly on zooplankton.
sections.behavior: Its migrations follow changing river levels: fish move upstream in some seasons and return downstream toward the delta and floodplain.
sections.reproduction: Mature, egg-bearing fish have been recorded moving upstream during the rising-water period, consistent with a seasonal spawning migration.
sections.ecology: Pelagic eggs and drifting larvae depend on river flow to reach nursery habitat, linking reproduction to an uninterrupted flood pulse.
sections.conservation: FishBase relays a global Least Concern assessment from 2011, while also recording local declines around the Khone Falls.
